related.search_scope: Searched astral-sh/uv open and closed issues and open, closed, and merged pull requests using authenticated gh. Literal searches covered "failed to create UnixStream", "Function not implemented", UnixStream, ENOSYS, SIGABRT, socketpair, i686/manylinux, ubuntu-26.04, and cibuildwheel. Conceptual searches covered 32-bit failures, container crashes, sockets, Tokio runtime initialization, and signals; separate cause-oriented searches covered seccomp and Docker permissions. Historical/fix searches included uv 0.13.6/0.13.7 crashes and merged runtime/platform changes. Included comments in targeted searches and inspected candidate discussions and linked historical PRs. PR text searches returned no matches; supplemented them by screening 1,500 recent PR titles across all states. Ruled out astral-sh/uv#22170 (nonblocking stderr/EAGAIN), astral-sh/uv#21935 (SIGPIPE forwarding), astral-sh/uv#9050 (disabled flock), astral-sh/uv#12433 (compiler memory exhaustion), and astral-sh/uv#2732 (iSH emulation crashes). The merged signal-forwarding change astral-sh/uv#13017 and open Docker-image change astral-sh/uv#23140 do not track this failure. No matching prior fix or existing regression tracker was found.

type_reason: The reported uv pip install process aborts with SIGABRT after UnixStream creation returns ENOSYS on Linux i686, a documented Tier 2 target. This is an operational failure, even though the responsible component and syscall remain unconfirmed. No existing issue or pull request was found that tracks the same failure. The container uv version is unknown, so the report does not establish a regression between uv 0.13.6 and 0.13.7 or a recurrence of a previously fixed bug.
summary: No closely related issue or pull request was found. Existing SIGABRT, UnixStream, ENOSYS, and i686 reports concern different operations or mechanisms; none establishes the cause of this container-specific abort.
draft_response: Linux i686 is a supported Tier 2 target. Your log shows uv aborting while creating a UnixStream, but it does not identify the failing syscall or establish a Docker/seccomp cause. Please capture `/usr/local/bin/uv --version` and `file /usr/local/bin/uv` inside the failing container; the host setup-uv version does not identify that binary. Then compare a minimal wheel install on ubuntu-24.04 and ubuntu-26.04 with the container digest and uv version pinned. If it still aborts, please share verbose output and a syscall trace covering socket creation. Comparing the default seccomp profile with `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` would also help test the filtering hypothesis.
